summary:
Most of this week's sessions went to homelab infrastructure: shipping and hardening a coordination proxy that serializes access to a shared GPU across multiple inference backends — text gen, image gen, and embeddings all competing for 16 GB of VRAM without OOM. The proxy was confirmed working end-to-end with a remote LAN client, and a model-name rewrite layer was added to keep the client's UI coherent when the text-gen backend has idle-unloaded.

The proxy's lock rule was also revised after some whack-a-mole with client probe paths triggering spurious reload storms. The fix: enumerate the specific mutating POSTs that actually touch GPU — everything else, including all GETs, bypasses the lock entirely. Five parallel version pings now return in 33ms instead of kicking off a 120s reload cycle.

On the phillipsben side, the daily dashboard refresh is stable. Phases 3 and 4 — Claude memory summaries and Spotify plumbing — are wired in, and this tile now updates each morning from the pop-os memory snapshot. (snapshot stale, last sync 2026-05-19)
